subject: Density as calculated by expected or average cluster size: Distance in Windows vs Distance in R

messages.author: 8028d75f27f06548
messages.subject: Density as calculated by expected or average cluster size: Distance in Windows vs Distance in R
parts:
Dear Helpful Distance Sampling People
As ever, i am enjoying and appreciating using distance sampling methods.

Please may i ask for clarification.
In Software Distance in Windows, i believe that the density calculation uses expected cluster size times by number of clusters to calculate density.

Please is this different in Package Distance in R.   
Does this instead use average cluster size times by number of clusters to calculate density. If that is the case, please is there a way to change how this is calculated in R so that it provides the same calculated results as in Software Distance in Windows. 

Thank you for considering.  With kind regards, Carlos

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Density as calculated by expected or average cluster size: Distance in Windows vs Distance in R
parts:
Carlos

Multiple questions packed in this email.

DistWin offers several choices when dealing with animals in groups. The sample project "Stratify example"  contains survey data from animals in groups. In the window below, you can produce density estimates of individuals by multiplying group density by mean of observed groups or use the size-bias regression to adjust the group size estimate to account for size bias.

Yet another method is to use group size as a covariate in the detection function. This can be done in DistWin by choosing the MCDS engine and making the appropriate selections in this window below:

You can get the "Distance" R package to use either average observed group size (as you indicate) or include group size as a covariate in the detection function. The "Distance" R package does not offer the size-bias regression option as the current suggested approach for handling size bias is to include group size as a covariate in the detection function, thus

clever.hn <- ds(data=risso, key="hn", formula = ~size)
I hope that answers your questions.

Dear Eric
Good to hear from you.   Yes, thank you, this has resolved my query.   I understand the differences now.   I have since tried in R using group size as a covariate, and this is giving me answers much closer (~3%) to the results from DistWin when using size biased regression.   Thank you so much for taking the time to explain this to me.  With kind regards, Carlos
